Builds good_v3.json: the dashboard's "How good is it?" tables (W-TOOL, run 3).

Error metric: RMSE as % of the naive guess (predict the TRAIN-split mean of labels_v2 for that endpoint),
on the TEST split (leak-free cluster split), overall and by nn_sim_train bin (<0.3, 0.3-0.5, 0.5-0.7, >=0.7;
nn_sim_train taken from labels_v2 by endpoint+full InChIKey). Methods are compared on the SAME rows: for each
endpoint, rows where every listed method has a prediction (EPI included when it has a value); pKa has no EPI.
Interval coverage: empirical fraction of test y inside [lo,hi], printed next to the nominal level.
Config: GOOD_CONFIG below (swap in the frozen model of the run by editing one path).
note: LEAK-FREE column first: test chemicals with Tanimoto < 0.40 to every training skeleton (W-SPACE quarantine_v3, canonical; fewer than 10 rows = not reported). The other columns use the whole cluster-held-out test set, which still contains near neighbours of training chemicals. Naive guess = training-set mean of each property (water solubility: miscibility-gated rows excluded, as in the model fit). 95% intervals: cluster bootstrap over test clusters (1000 reps). A method is called better or worse than EPI Suite only when the 95% interval of the paired difference excludes 0; otherwise not resolved. Same test chemicals for every method in a row block. Identity here: one row per full standardized InChIKey (stereo kept), the same key as the paper (run 4 fix after CRITIC audit; earlier builds merged stereoisomers on the first InChIKey block). nn_sim = highest Tanimoto (Morgan r2) similarity to any training compound. EPI Suite has no intervals.

spectra.note: Spectrum-only models by ion block (W-SPECTRA spectrum_only_v31). The bins are the STRUCTURAL novelty of the test compounds. Mass + adduct only shows what the fragments add; "known structure, same compounds" shows the gap to having the structure. Spectral similarity was found UNINFORMATIVE about error for HR-ESI, so no novelty tag is shown on spectrum-only predictions. LEAK-FREE column (ESI only; W-SPECTRA leak_free_v31.csv, deployed single-spectrum model): states only whether its 95% CI stays below 100% of naive. DISPUTED, left open: how many endpoints a spectrum alone has skill for differs between our deliverables (3 or 4, scored on different models under different bars); this column is not a verdict on that count. EI has no leak-free check. Spectrum-only intervals under-cover on unseen chemistry (empirical 0.81-0.96 at nominal 0.90). These are the models this page runs; the paper's spectral ablation used separate W-MODEL v5 models, so its numbers differ.
